spec.title: Refuse checkout when stock levels cannot be read
spec.need: When stock enforcement is on, a shopper cannot buy an item that is out of stock by taking advantage of an inventory service error.
acceptanceCriteria: With stock enforcement on, when the stock level of an item cannot be read, the checkout is refused and the shopper sees that stock is temporarily unavailable.
The refusal is logged as one record that names the order and the cause; the log format is unchanged.
With stock enforcement off, an inventory service error does not block checkouts.
An order whose items are all in stock with a readable inventory is not affected.
outOfScope: Turning stock enforcement on in production.
spec.expectedProof: A test that simulates an inventory service error with enforcement on: the checkout is accepted on main and refused on the branch.

checks.description: With stock enforcement on and the inventory raising an OSError or a database error, the checkout ends with a refusal telling the shopper that stock is temporarily unavailable.
The refused checkout emits exactly one warning-or-higher log record that names the order and the cause, with the usual record fields.
With stock enforcement off or absent, an inventory error lets the checkout through.
With enforcement on, an order whose stock is readable and sufficient is accepted with no warning logged.
